newsitem.title: USA: Offshore drillers' earnings seen racing ahead.
newsitem.headline: Offshore drillers' earnings seen racing ahead.

text.p: A rapid expansion in oil and gas companies' exploration and drilling programs will provide a stimulus to second quarter and full year earnings, and there could be surprises on the upside, according to analysts.

"Heading into the second quarter reporting season, we expect strong earnings from our offshore drilling universe to continue and believe at current prices, the valuations in the group are compelling," said Carol Lau, analyst at Oppenheimer & Co.
Lau expects a "significant" upside surprise for Ensco International, with earnings per share of $0.72, against a First Call consensus estimate of $0.65.

Lau cut her earnings estimate for Transocean Offshore Inc to $0.55 per share from $0.61 after the company said it expected earnings to be $0.10 below analysts' forecasts of $0.65 due to higher levels of delays in commencing new contracts.

"There are always going to be issues affecting individual companies such as Transocean, while Reading & Bates Co will take a charge related to a dry hole," said Ravi Kamath, analyst at Jefferies & Co.
The past month has seen companies announce a series of long-term contracts at higher rates as the global offshore fleet is close to full capacity utilization.
"You see companies like Ensco which have all of their North Sea jackups leased on an indexed monthly rate, so they benefit immediately from any rate rises," said Kamath.
Lau said Noble Drilling Corp may come in below second quarter forecasts because of an accounting issue related to the sale of the company's mat-supported rig fleet.
However, for the sector as a whole, she is bullish on full-year and 1998 earnings and says peak earnings for the sector are still some three years away.
The sector was frightened earlier this year when analysts saw evidence of new building that could end the rapid expansion in dayrates that has been seen this year and last.

Lau forecasts dayrates of $95,000-$105,000 for new semi-submersible contracts in the Gulf of Mexico, which account for 30 percent of global demand, up from $80,000-$90,000 recently. And a Gulf of Mexico lease sale in August will provide a further filip to drilling and exploration activities.

"Through 2000, we forecast uninterrupted double-digit annual earnings growth for those companies positioned in the deepwater and premium jackup rigs, assuming oil prices average above $18 per barrel and gas prices average above $1.80 per thousand cubic feet annually," Lau said.
